controls.title: Back up critical information and systems
controls.statement: Back up data, applications and configuration needed to restore business services. Set and operate schedules and retention periods based on business needs and applicable requirements.
controls.risk: Missing or incomplete backups could leave the organisation unable to recover important information after an outage or attack.
controls.scope: Business data, application components and configuration needed for recovery.
controls.examine: Compare service inventories and recovery needs with backup schedules, retained copies and job results.
controls.interview: Ask service owners how backup scope and acceptable data loss are agreed, and operators how failed jobs are resolved.
controls.test: Sample critical services and verify successful backups cover all required components. Compare actual backup dates and retention with the approved requirements.
test_steps: Select critical services and enumerate the data, configuration, software, credentials and dependencies required to restore each one.
Compare that set with backup policies, schedules, successful job records, retention and the most recent recoverable copy.
Inspect failed, partial and missed jobs and verify alerts reached an owner, retries or corrective actions completed and protection gaps were assessed.
Choose source records created before and after a backup boundary and confirm the retained copy aligns with the approved recovery-point requirement.
controls.expected: Required components are covered; backup frequency and retention meet documented needs and source-specific minimums, and failures are resolved.

mappings.basis: Requires backups and retention based on business criticality and continuity requirements.
Requires automated backups at least weekly; verify automation and cadence separately.
Addresses backup scope and frequency; also assess documentation backups and protection requirements.

controls.title: Protect and isolate recovery copies
controls.statement: Protect backup copies against unauthorised access, alteration and deletion. Maintain a recovery copy separated from threats affecting the live environment.
controls.risk: An attacker or equipment failure could destroy both live information and its backups, leaving no reliable way to recover.
controls.scope: Backup storage, administrative identities and isolated recovery copies.
controls.examine: Inspect backup access permissions, isolation arrangements, encryption where required and deletion protections.
controls.interview: Ask the backup owner which failures or account compromises could affect both production and recovery copies.
controls.test: Use authorised test records to verify access restrictions and deletion protection. Confirm that an isolated copy remains available when the primary environment is unavailable.
test_steps: Select recovery copies across critical platforms and verify encryption, access control, administrative separation, deletion protection and retention against policy.
Using an authorised non-backup administrator, attempt to list, alter and delete a test copy and its policy; confirm the actions fail or trigger immediate alerting.
Simulate loss of the primary environment in an isolated test and verify at least one protected copy remains reachable through separately controlled recovery credentials.
Review changes to backup policy and administrative permissions and confirm they are centrally logged and reviewed independently of the production administrators.
controls.expected: Recovery copies have appropriate protection and a tested separation from production failure or compromise; additional source-specific safeguards are verified.

mappings.basis: Requires secure and resilient retention of backups.
Specifically requires technically enforced immutability throughout retention; isolation alone is insufficient.
Protect recovery data with equivalent controls to original data, subject to its requirements.
Requires an isolated instance of recovery data.
Requires specified critical copies in a separate facility or non-collocated fire-rated container; verify the physical arrangement.

controls.title: Demonstrate recovery from backups
controls.statement: Test restoration of information, applications and configuration together. Verify the restored service works and measure recovery time and data loss against agreed objectives.
controls.risk: Backups that cannot restore a working service could prolong an outage and cause permanent loss of information.
controls.scope: Representative business services, their dependencies and agreed recovery objectives.
controls.examine: Inspect restore exercises, selected backup dates, data integrity checks and measured recovery results.
controls.interview: Ask service owners how they confirm the recovered service is usable and how unresolved test failures are tracked.
controls.test: Witness an authorised restore in an isolated environment. Check that related components reach a consistent point in time and compare service recovery and data loss with agreed objectives.
test_steps: Choose a critical service and an approved recovery point without relying on the production team to preselect an easy backup.
Restore data, configuration and dependent components into an isolated environment using the documented procedure and authorised recovery identities.
Run integrity and business-function checks, reconcile record counts or transactions and measure actual restoration time and data loss against approved objectives.
Record manual interventions, failed steps and undocumented dependencies, then trace corrective actions to owners and a scheduled retest.
controls.expected: The recovered service is usable, information is consistent and recovery objectives are met; test frequency satisfies applicable source conditions.

mappings.basis: Requires restoration to a common point in time during disaster recovery exercises.
Requires recovery testing at least quarterly for a sample of assets; verify frequency and sample coverage.
Demonstrates recovery to a known state within defined objectives; backup restoration may not cover every reconstitution activity.
